launch-pa-pittsburgh-schenley-park.summary: A 456-acre Oakland park linking wooded trails, Panther Hollow, Flagstaff Hill, Schenley Plaza, sports facilities and Phipps Conservatory.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-schenley-park.hours: City park areas are generally open 6:00 a.m. to sunset when unlighted and until 11:00 p.m. where lighted. Phipps, the pool and golf course use separate schedules.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-schenley-park.parking: Parking is distributed among Schenley Plaza meters, Panther Hollow and Overlook drives, facility lots and Oakland streets. Route to the exact destination; university events change availability.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-schenley-park.arrival: Use Schenley Plaza for Phipps and the north end, Overlook Drive for the Oval and pool, or Panther Hollow Road for the lake and lower trails.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-schenley-park.restrooms: Dependable restrooms are inside Phipps and staffed recreation facilities during their hours; trail areas do not guarantee one.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-schenley-park.cost: Grounds, trails, plaza and overlooks are free. Phipps, golf, pool, rentals, food and events may cost separately.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-schenley-park.accessibility: The plaza and many facility approaches are paved, but the park is steep and wooded trails and Panther Hollow are uneven.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-schenley-park.dogs: Leashed dogs are welcome outdoors but not in Phipps, pools, playground equipment or posted facilities.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-schenley-park.family: The plaza, Phipps, pool, Oval and slopes offer varied family stops, but choose one destination before arrival.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-schenley-park.transit: Frequent buses serve Oakland and Schenley Plaza; lower areas require a downhill walk and uphill return.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-schenley-park.need: Do not use one generic park pin. Pick Phipps, the plaza, Flagstaff Hill, Panther Hollow or the Oval first.

launch-pa-pittsburgh-frick-park.summary: Pittsburgh's largest historic regional park is a network of separate arrival zones: the free Frick Environmental Center, Blue Slide Playground, wooded ravine trails, the Upper Frick off-leash area, red-clay courts, fields and the restored Nine Mile Run corridor.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-frick-park.hours: City parks normally operate 6:00 a.m.-11:00 p.m., although unlighted facilities and natural trails can close at sunset or under posted conditions. The Frick Environmental Center's published building schedule is Monday-Friday 9:00 a.m.-5:00 p.m., Saturday 10:00 a.m.-6:00 p.m. and Sunday noon-5:00 p.m.; verify same-day building and event notices.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-frick-park.parking: Do not navigate only to the broad park pin. The Environmental Center has its own parking at 2005 Beechwood Boulevard; Blue Slide uses the 2466 Beechwood Boulevard and English Lane approach; Forbes and Braddock serve the playground, fields and red-clay courts; Nine Mile Run uses Commercial Street or Duck Hollow arrival areas. Construction can close trail lots and change through-routes.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-frick-park.arrival: Start at the Environmental Center for maps, bathrooms, water and a gentler developed introduction. Use Blue Slide's Beechwood Boulevard entrance for the iconic hillside playground, and use the exact Nine Mile Run destination only after checking the active Commercial Street Bridge project detours.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-frick-park.restrooms: The most dependable documented restrooms and water fountains are at the Frick Environmental Center during building hours. City recreation buildings and portable toilets near Blue Slide or fields are not guaranteed daily; use a confirmed facility before entering the ravines or Nine Mile Run corridor.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-frick-park.cost: Park grounds, trails, playgrounds, the designated dog area and ordinary Environmental Center access are free. Classes, camps, private rentals, permits and reserved recreation may charge separately.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-frick-park.accessibility: The Environmental Center provides the strongest developed arrival with parking, bathrooms and firm routes, but the park's ravines include steep grades, mud, roots, gravel and uneven trail surfaces. A 2026 City project is separately evaluating Environmental Center ADA upgrades, so check posted routing when step-free access is essential.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-frick-park.dogs: Dogs must remain leashed except inside the signed Upper Frick Off-Leash Exercise Area. Dogs are prohibited from playgrounds and courts; keep them on marked routes and out of sensitive restoration habitat.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-frick-park.family: For a first family visit, pair the Environmental Center with a short nearby nature route or go directly to Blue Slide Playground at the Beechwood Boulevard and Nicholson Street side. The Environmental Center has bathrooms and water; ravine and Nine Mile Run trips require trail footwear, close supervision and a return climb.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-frick-park.transit: The Environmental Center guide identifies bus 65 at Darlington and Beechwood and routes 61A and 61B at Forbes and Dallas. Choose transit for the intended park edge because Blue Slide, Forbes and Braddock, the Environmental Center and Nine Mile Run are not one compact arrival area.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-frick-park.need: Download the official Frick map before entering the ravines. The Commercial Street Bridge replacement is actively affecting Nine Mile Run access in 2026, including closures between trail parking areas; check PennDOT and posted detours before planning a through-walk or ride. Trails can also become muddy, icy or flood-prone after weather.

launch-pa-pittsburgh-point-state-park.address: 601 Commonwealth Place, Building A, Pittsburgh, PA 15222
launch-pa-pittsburgh-point-state-park.summary: Point State Park is Pittsburgh's 36-acre state park at the Forks of the Ohio, combining the iconic fountain, paved riverfront promenades, fort outlines, modern restrooms, the paid Fort Pitt Museum and the free Fort Pitt Block House.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-point-state-park.hours: Park grounds are open every day of the year from sunrise to sunset, and day-use areas close at dusk. The paid Commonwealth Place lot operates 6:00 a.m.-11:00 p.m.; the museum, Block House, fountain, concession and events keep separate schedules.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-point-state-park.parking: The operator-managed lot along Commonwealth Place charges a fee and has a separate 6:00 a.m.-11:00 p.m. schedule. Limited metered parking and a visitor drop-off are near the entrance, while downtown garages provide alternatives; major events can close or reprice roads and parking.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-point-state-park.arrival: For a first visit, enter from Commonwealth Place, cross beneath the Portal Bridge, then choose the museum and Block House near the entrance or continue west across the lawn to the fountain and river confluence. Do not navigate only to the fountain if you need parking or indoor facilities.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-point-state-park.restrooms: DCNR documents modern restrooms and potable water as trailhead amenities inside the park, and the official map places them near the entrance and park office rather than at the fountain tip. Fort Pitt Museum also has an accessible first-floor restroom during admission hours.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-point-state-park.cost: Pennsylvania state parks charge no entrance or day-use fee. The grounds, fountain, fort outlines and Fort Pitt Block House are free; parking and Fort Pitt Museum admission cost separately, and food or events may add charges.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-point-state-park.accessibility: DCNR identifies the riverfront promenades, overlooks, amphitheaters and fishing access as accessible. The main routes are paved, but event fencing, crowds, weather and maintenance can alter circulation; the museum has an automatic entrance, elevator and accessible first-floor restroom.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-point-state-park.dogs: Pets are permitted in state-park day-use areas unless posted closed, but they must remain physically controlled and attended. Ordinary pets may not enter park buildings or museums; ADA-defined service animals are welcomed by Fort Pitt Museum.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-point-state-park.family: The fountain, river traffic, fort footprints and free Block House make a flexible outdoor family visit. The museum adds indoor exhibits and children ages 17 and under receive free general admission but still need tickets; supervise closely beside the rivers and fountain basin.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-point-state-park.transit: The T light-rail system is free within Downtown and the North Shore, and downtown buses stop within walking distance. The Three Rivers Heritage Trail and Great Allegheny Passage also reach the park, making transit or walking useful during major events.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-point-state-park.need: Large events can fully close or reconfigure the park, lot and riverfront paths. The fountain is ornamental and not a splash pad or swimming area; verify DCNR alerts, fountain operation, museum tickets and Block House hours before relying on a specific facility.

launch-pa-pittsburgh-highland-park.address: Highland Avenue and Reservoir Drive, Pittsburgh, PA 15206
launch-pa-pittsburgh-highland-park.summary: Highland Park is a large East End destination organized around its formal entry garden and reservoir, with separate playground, pool, courts, volleyball, cycling-track and Pittsburgh Zoo arrival zones.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-highland-park.hours: City park areas generally follow posted park hours, with unlighted natural areas best used in daylight. Highland Park Pool, Pittsburgh Zoo, concerts, movies, reserved shelters and recreation facilities keep separate seasonal or event schedules.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-highland-park.parking: For the fountain, gardens and reservoir, use legal spaces around Highland Avenue and Reservoir Drive and read posted restrictions. The pool, playgrounds, Bud Harris Cycling Track and zoo are spread across different edges; zoo visitors should navigate to the free main lot at 7370 Baker Street.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-highland-park.arrival: Use Highland Avenue for the formal Entry Garden and continue uphill toward Reservoir Drive for the reservoir loop. Route directly to 151 Lake Drive for the pool or 7370 Baker Street for the zoo; one broad park pin is not a practical arrival for every facility.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-highland-park.restrooms: Do not assume an always-open restroom at the garden or reservoir loop. The pool has facilities only during its seasonal operating hours, and zoo restrooms require zoo access; use a confirmed staffed facility before starting a longer walk.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-highland-park.cost: The park grounds, entry garden, reservoir views, playgrounds, courts and ordinary paths are free. The zoo charges admission, the pool may require a daily pass or membership, and food, programs, shelter reservations and special events can cost separately.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-highland-park.accessibility: Reservoir Drive improvements added traffic calming and accessibility work, and the entry garden and reservoir area include paved approaches. Grades remain significant between zones; the zoo publishes separate mobility, sensory, restroom and rental guidance.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-highland-park.dogs: Leashed dogs may use ordinary outdoor park areas under City rules, but keep them out of playground equipment, pools, courts and posted facilities. The Pittsburgh Zoo prohibits personal animals, including in the parking lot; ADA-defined service animals follow the zoo's separate policy.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-highland-park.family: For a free family visit, pair the fountain and reservoir with a chosen playground rather than trying to cover every zone. The Super Playground, Farmhouse Playground, Pool Grove Playground and Rhododendron Playground are separate facilities; the pool and zoo each require their own schedule and arrival plan.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-highland-park.transit: Pittsburgh Regional Transit serves Highland Avenue and the zoo area, but stops are not interchangeable across this large hillside park. Plan the final walking grade to the garden, reservoir, pool or Baker Street zoo entrance before choosing a route.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-highland-park.need: The reservoir is not a swimming area; it is drinking-water infrastructure and not a wading destination. Pool hours change seasonally, zoo construction is altering internal circulation through spring 2027, and summer concerts or movies can increase traffic around Reservoir Drive; check the exact operator before leaving.

launch-pa-pittsburgh-riverview-park.summary: Riverview Park is Pittsburgh's steep, wooded North Side regional park, organized around the Visitor Center entrance, Observatory Hill, reservable Chapel Shelter, seasonal pool, playground, courts, off-leash area, overlooks and natural trails.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-riverview-park.hours: City park areas generally follow posted park hours, with unlighted woods and trails best used in daylight. The Allegheny Observatory is open only for scheduled programming, Chapel Shelter is permit-controlled, and Riverview Pool keeps a separate seasonal schedule; verify the exact facility before leaving.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-riverview-park.parking: Parking is distributed rather than concentrated at one entrance. Use the Visitor Center and Observatory Hill arrival for orientation and scheduled observatory events, the signed Chapel Ridge drive for the Chapel or pool, and a named trailhead for hiking; do not assume one small lot serves the entire park.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-riverview-park.arrival: For a first visit, navigate to the Visitor Center at 1 Riverview Avenue. The Observatory is across the entrance road and uphill, while the pool and Chapel Shelter are farther along Riverview Drive; Valley Refuge and the Mairdale trail network are separate arrivals in steep terrain.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-riverview-park.restrooms: Do not assume an always-open trail restroom. Riverview Pool has facilities only during seasonal pool hours, and Chapel Shelter's indoor restrooms are part of a permitted rental. Confirm a staffed facility before starting a longer hike.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-riverview-park.cost: Park grounds, trails, playground, courts, overlooks and the designated off-leash area are free. Observatory public tours are free but require reservations; pool admission, shelter permits, food and some programs use separate terms. The current Chapel permit fee is $375.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-riverview-park.accessibility: The entrance, developed recreation areas and Chapel Shelter have firmer approaches, but grades are significant and many trails are natural, muddy, rooted or uneven. The historic Observatory is only partially accessible; contact its operator before reserving when an accommodation is essential.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-riverview-park.dogs: Dogs must remain leashed except inside the signed year-round Riverview Park off-leash exercise area behind Observatory Hill. Keep dogs out of playgrounds, pools, courts, reservable interiors and posted natural-restoration zones.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-riverview-park.family: The playground and seasonal pool are the easiest child-focused stops, while the Visitor Center is a useful ranger-program meeting point. Observatory events require advance registration, and natural-trail outings need closed-toe shoes, water and close supervision on steep or muddy sections.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-riverview-park.transit: Transit serves Perrysville Avenue and streets around the park, but the Observatory, Chapel Ridge, Grand Avenue and Mairdale entrances are not interchangeable. Plan the final grade and walk to the exact destination before choosing a stop.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-riverview-park.need: The Observatory is not an always-open walk-in attraction, and its 2026 public-tour registration is currently full with a waiting list and possible added September dates. Stars at Riverview concerts and movies can change Observatory Hill traffic; trail conditions, pool operation and permit-controlled buildings should be checked separately.

launch-pa-pittsburgh-emerald-view-park.summary: A Mount Washington network of overlooks, wooded hillsides, neighborhood parks, greenways and trails with iconic downtown views.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-emerald-view-park.hours: Park and overlook areas are generally open 6:00 a.m. to sunset when unlighted and until 11:00 p.m. where lighted. Use trails in daylight.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-emerald-view-park.parking: Grandview Avenue has limited curb parking; neighborhood parks and trailheads have separate small parking zones.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-emerald-view-park.arrival: Navigate to a named Grandview overlook for skyline views or a specific trailhead for hiking.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-emerald-view-park.restrooms: There is no dependable restroom at every overlook or trailhead; plan around open neighborhood facilities.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-emerald-view-park.cost: Overlooks, trails, playgrounds and park areas are free.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-emerald-view-park.accessibility: Grandview sidewalks and selected overlooks are paved; hillside trails are steep, narrow and uneven.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-emerald-view-park.dogs: Leashed dogs are welcome; use caution on steep edges and clean up in residential areas.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-emerald-view-park.family: Overlooks and playgrounds are easy family stops; hillside hikes suit trail-ready children rather than strollers.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-emerald-view-park.transit: Inclines and Mount Washington buses reduce driving but still require a walk to individual destinations.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-emerald-view-park.need: This is not one contiguous lawn. Use named destinations and avoid steep muddy slopes after storms.

launch-pa-pittsburgh-mellon-park.summary: An East End park combining a historic walled garden with playground, seasonal spray park, tennis center, fields and public art.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-mellon-park.hours: City park areas are generally open 6:00 a.m. to sunset when unlighted and until 11:00 p.m. where lighted. Spray and tennis operations are seasonal.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-mellon-park.parking: Use curb parking on Beechwood, Fifth or Shady, observing restrictions. Entrances serve different park levels.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-mellon-park.arrival: Shady Avenue serves the garden and lower park; Beechwood and Fifth better serve some recreation areas.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-mellon-park.restrooms: Restrooms are most likely near staffed tennis or recreation facilities during their hours.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-mellon-park.cost: Park, gardens, playground, field and spray play are free; tennis programs may cost separately.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-mellon-park.accessibility: Major areas have paved approaches, but terraces, stairs and grades mean entrances are not equivalent.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-mellon-park.dogs: Leashed dogs are welcome outside the spray park, playground, courts and garden beds.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-mellon-park.family: The playground, seasonal spray park and field pair well with the quieter walled garden.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-mellon-park.transit: Buses serve Fifth, Shady and nearby corridors; choose the stop closest to the entrance.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-mellon-park.need: The spray park is seasonal and weather-dependent. Verify operation and choose the right entrance for mobility needs.

launch-pa-pittsburgh-north-shore-riverfr.summary: A riverfront promenade linking PNC Park, Acrisure Stadium, water steps, public art, trails, docks, museums and downtown bridges.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-north-shore-riverfr.hours: Outdoor riverfront areas generally follow city park rules. Water steps, docks, museums and stadium grounds have separate schedules or closures.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-north-shore-riverfr.parking: Garages and lots are paid and event-priced. On game or concert days, reserve ahead or use transit.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-north-shore-riverfr.arrival: Choose PNC Park, Acrisure Stadium, Water Steps or Carnegie Science Center as the arrival anchor; walking from downtown is often simplest.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-north-shore-riverfr.restrooms: Dependable restrooms are inside staffed attractions during their hours; the open riverwalk does not guarantee late-night facilities.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-north-shore-riverfr.cost: Paths, lawns, Water Steps and public art are free. Parking, museums, events, cruises and food cost separately.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-north-shore-riverfr.accessibility: The main riverwalk is paved and mostly level, with ramps at key connections; events can alter routes.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-north-shore-riverfr.dogs: Leashed dogs are welcome on ordinary paths but may be restricted near events and security zones.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-north-shore-riverfr.family: Water Steps, river traffic, public art and the science center make a strong family corridor; supervise beside water.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-north-shore-riverfr.transit: North Side light rail and buses serve the district; downtown bridges provide pedestrian access.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-north-shore-riverfr.need: Stadium schedules dominate parking, prices and closures. Check both venues and Water Steps operation before driving.
